verdict.rationale: Gmail's own docs show search operators that can be combined to narrow results, and a search can be turned into a filter. One community user also reports searching a large archive easily. Nothing in the pack addresses search speed, result ranking, or explicit coverage of the full mail history. missing for 10: evidence of fast search performance, ranked or relevance-ordered results, explicit full-history search coverage, independent hands-on corroboration of precision.

support.subject: As a power-user, search is fast and precise — operators, filters, and ranked results across my full mail history

citations.quote: You can use words or symbols called search operators to filter your Gmail search results. You can also combine operators to filter your results even more.
After you search, you can use the results to set up a filter for these messages.
To search for snoozed emails, at the top, in the search bar, enter `in:snoozed`.
